choices.ensemble: Sustained polyphonic synthesis, environmental sampler layers and soft synthesized percussion foreground atmosphere while retaining techno-derived pulse.
choices.parts: Jupiter-8 polyphonic-pad lineage and sampled field-workflow are authored catalog equivalents. Sine kick, hissy snare/hat and gentle swing represent subdued pulses.
choices.chain: Stereo XY field capture/portable preamp plus DAW summing, gentle optics, tilt EQ, tape-echo character and wide stereo reverb/panning are authored equivalents. No claim that Sommer used these named devices or this exact signal path.
choices.axes: Authored full13: one harmonic field, fixed temperament, plain melodic detail, mildly metrical changing pulse, moderate layers, lower intensity, no singing, neutral grain, subordinate percussion, cyclic evolution. Transmission neutral.
choices.room: Auteur home studio models assembly and processing of field material; it is not an asserted physical room on the album.

neighbors.distinction: Environmental atmospheres carry a principal voice above the soft beat instead of compact chord-and-kick dub tools.
Techno pulse and synthetic palette, without prescribing reggae riddim tuning, live bass and melodica.
Specifically dub-processing space and environmental sampling rather than all listening-techno.

choices.ensemble: Patchable synth and synthesized drum voices form two editable catalog chairs. Their roles can share one real rack; the partition does not assert two specific physical boxes.

choices.chain: Uncompressed line capture, parametric shaping and a digital/DAW finish are authored model choices. Hardware module identity, mic/preamp brand and exact session chain are not attested.
choices.axes: Authored full13: minimal harmonic progression, sequenced pitch, strict base pulse, timbral density, high real-time generativity, synthesized rough grain, foreground drums and cyclical figures. Transmission neutral.
choices.room: Auteur home studio represents the performer-controlled patch and recording process.

neighbors.distinction: Patch-generation and improvisation define the practice; extreme distortion is optional.
Technique and performance workflow rather than a single atmospheric arrangement aesthetic.
Live timbral intervention and synthesized percussive variability, without requiring extreme subtraction.
